cards.text: We pick up Samson's story again, friend. Samson, Israel's judge, is on the move. One day he goes to Gaza and spends the night with a prostitute there.

The people of Gaza hear Samson's in town, so they surround the place and wait for him all night at the city gate. Not a peep out of them, like me in the junk drawer whenever somebody came digging for the good scissors.

cards.question: The people of Gaza plan to wait until dawn and then kill Samson.

cards.text: But Samson only stays until midnight. Then he gets up and heads for the city gate.

cards.question: It's midnight in Gaza, and Samson is at the city gate. What does he do?
Samson pulls out the doors of Gaza's city gate but leaves the gateposts behind.

cards.text: He puts the doors, the gateposts and the bar on his shoulders and carries them to the top of the mountain overlooking Hebron. Friend, I get winded carrying ONE full cookie box across my bakery!
Some time later, Samson falls in love with a woman in the Valley of Sorek named Delilah. Then the lords of the Philistines, their rulers, come to her with an offer.

cards.question: The lords of the Philistines want Delilah to find out something about Samson. What is it?

answers.text: Where his great strength comes from
When he plans to attack next

cards.question: What do the lords of the Philistines offer Delilah if she finds out Samson's secret?

answers.text: A house in the Valley of Sorek

cards.text: That's eleven hundred from EACH lord, friend. So Delilah skips the small talk and asks Samson, "Please tell me the source of your great strength and how you can be tied up and subdued."

cards.question: Samson tells Delilah that if they tie him up with seven fresh bowstrings, he'll become as ___ as any other man.

cards.text: So the lords bring Delilah seven fresh bowstrings, and she ties Samson up with them. Men are hiding in her room when she calls out, "Samson, the Philistines are here!"

cards.question: Samson's tied up with seven fresh bowstrings, and Delilah just called out that the Philistines are here. What happens?

answers.text: He gives up without a fight

cards.question: After the bowstrings snap, Delilah finally knows the source of Samson's strength.

cards.text: Delilah tells Samson he's mocked her and lied to her, and she asks again. This time he says new ropes that have never been used will make him weak.

cards.question: Delilah ties Samson up with brand-new ropes and calls out that the Philistines are here. What happens?

answers.text: He snaps them off his arms
He slips out and runs off

cards.text: Bowstrings: snapped. Ropes: snapped. Delilah tells Samson he's mocked her and lied to her all along, and she asks one more time.

cards.question: On Delilah's third try, what does Samson tell her will make him weak?

answers.text: Weaving his braids into a loom
Locking him in an iron cage

cards.text: So while Samson sleeps, Delilah weaves his seven braids into the web and tightens it with a pin. Then she calls out again, "Samson, the Philistines are here!"

cards.question: Samson wakes up and pulls out the pin, along with the loom and the web.

cards.text: Delilah asks him, "How can you say, 'I love you,'" and then, "when your heart is not with me?" She says this is the third time he's mocked her.

cards.question: How often does Delilah press Samson with her words?

cards.text: Every day. EVERY. DAY. She pleads until he's sick to death, and finally Samson tells her all that's in his heart.

cards.question: Samson finally tells Delilah his secret. What does he say about himself?

answers.text: His hair has never been cut

cards.question: Samson tells Delilah he has been a ___ to God from his mother's womb, and if he's shaved, his strength will leave him.
Delilah isn't sure Samson told the truth this time, so she waits before sending for the Philistine lords.

cards.text: Delilah sends for the lords, and they come with the money in their hands. She lulls Samson to sleep on her lap and calls a man to shave off his seven braids.

cards.question: While Samson sleeps on Delilah's lap, a man shaves off his seven braids. What happens to Samson's strength?

cards.text: Then she calls out, "Samson, the Philistines are here!" He wakes up and thinks, "I will escape as I did before and shake myself free."

cards.question: Samson thinks he'll shake himself free like before. But what doesn't he know?

answers.text: The LORD had departed from him
The lords had brought more men

cards.text: He didn't know. And the Philistines seize him, gouge out his eyes and bring him down to Gaza.

cards.question: In Gaza, Samson is bound with bronze ___ and forced to grind grain in the ___.
After it's shaved, the hair of Samson's head begins to grow back.

cards.text: Hold that thought right there, friend. Samson's story isn't finished yet.

findings.problem: Card 9's question tells the baker, in Samson's own words, that if he's shaved his strength will leave him. Three cards later, card 12 asks what happens to Samson's strength when he's shaved, and the answer is 'It leaves him.' Card 9 gives that answer away before card 12 asks it. Fix: end card 9's question after 'from his mother's womb', or drop or replace card 12.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The wrong answers don't fit the blanks. 'Bound with bronze shields' makes no sense, and 'temple' and 'palace' can't go in the first blank either. That leaves 'shackles' as the only word that works in blank 1, so the baker can find it by ruling the others out. Each wrong answer should be a believable fit for one of the blanks.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: Stop 2's story cards are almost all plain retelling. The only attempt at a laugh is 'Every day. EVERY. DAY.' (card 7). Delilah's third try (cards 1 and 3) and her 'How can you say I love you' line (card 5) can carry a real laugh at Samson's human situation without muddying a fact. Cards 19 to 21 can stay serious.

rule.text: Because he talks naturally, the funny moments come up a lot: in his reactions, his comparisons, his disbelief and his self-deprecation. When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
